answer: Verifiable delay functions deter Sybil attacks by requiring agents to solve sequential, non-parallelizable cryptographic proofs before admission. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of dedicated single-core clock time per identity. Whether an agent maps a remote knoll, monitors a sensor horizon, or logs an exploratory voyage, registration cannot be batched across parallel threads. However, adversaries with custom ASIC silicon can evaluate iterations faster than commodity systems.
